paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness web plugin that adds a LAN access
# dsh-lan-access
A DeepSeek Harness Web plugin that adds an explicit local IP selection and **LAN access** toggle to
Settings → General. Requires Node.js 22.19+ or 24+.
> **Tested with DeepSeek Harness `v0.2.1-rc.2`** (the current release) — peers `^0.2.1-rc.2`.
- **On** — binds one selected IPv4 or IPv6 address assigned to this machine. Other devices can use t

hat address; the loopback listener is replaced.
- **Off** — binds `127.0.0.1` (loopback only).
- Wil
dcard addresses such as `0.0.0.0` and `::` are never used. Loopback, scoped IPv6, link-local IPv4/IP
v6 (`169.254.x`, `fe80::/10`), and OS-reported temporary/deprecated IPv6 privacy addresses are exclu
ded from the selector, so it lists only usable LAN endpoints; IPv4 addresses come first.
## Migrating saved LAN settings
An older `$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json` containing only `{"enabled": true}` starts on loopback and repo
rts that an address must be selected. The file remains unchanged until you apply a setting. Open the
local GUI, select a local IP in Settings → General, and enable LAN access again.
[该节后续省略]

## How it works
| Half | File | Role |
| Host | `src/index.ts` | Owns a plugin-local persisted flag (`$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json`), the fenc
ed `/lan-access` JSON route (GET state / POST set), a loopback-only `/lan-access/handoff` that mints
the tokenized target URL before the rebind, the bind controller, and the `lanAccess` bind-host serv
ice. The webserver row's composed `host` expression reads that service, so every webserver (re)start
— boot, toggle, or a post-boot user-patch re-apply — converges to the persisted setting. A toggle r
estarts the webserver fiber only when the bind differs, using `fiber.update(config, noSave)`: the no
-save path keeps the composed tree out of `cordis.yml`, which would otherwise trigger an HMR subtree

reload. |
| Client | `src/client/` | Registers the General-settings row (`settings.general.item`, o
rder 15) with a native-styled switch, the concrete IPv4/IPv6 selector, the bound listener URL and co
py button, and zh/en copy. A same-origin restart is polled; when the bind moves away from the curren
t origin (which can never reconnect) the row navigates to the tokenized new address automatically, r
eplacing the stuck DSH reconnect loop. |
The route fence accepts loopback, the listener's concrete bind IP, or the deployment's trusted autho
rities read live from the connection row's resolved config. Cross-site requests are refused.
## Limitations

- **Disabling from a remote machine cannot reconnect that page.** The listener
returns to `127.0.0.1

`, which only exists on the server machine, so the
remote tab keeps retrying a dead origin. Re-enabl

e from the server machine
(or the loopback page); the row states this when it applies.
- **The autom

atic handoff is loopback-only.** The process launch token is
minted into the target URL only for a l

oopback page, so it never leaks to a
remote LAN browser. A bind change started from a non-loopback p

age (rare —
the selector is disabled while enabled) falls back to the plain address
link, and you mu

st supply the launch token printed by `dsh web`.
- **A fresh browser on the new origin needs the lau

nch token.** The URL shown
in the row omits `?token=`, by design. The automatic handoff carries it o

nly
for the page that performed the switch.
- **One concrete address, never a wildcard.** The listen

er binds exactly one
selected IPv4/IPv6 address; `0.0.0.0`, `::`, link-local, and OS-temporary
IPv6

addresses are never offered. Change the selection by disabling first.
- **Other tabs on the old orig

in do not follow.** Only the page that toggles
navigates to the new origin. Any other tab still open

on the old address
keeps retrying until it is refreshed at the new address or closed.
- **A saved a

ddress that disappears fails visibly.** If the machine loses the
selected interface (network change,

VPN drop, IPv6 privacy rotation), startup
refuses the bind instead of falling back to another inter

face. Set
`"enabled": false` in `$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json`, restart locally, and
reselect an availa

enabled": false` in `$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json`, restart locally, and
reselect an available address.
### Harness compatibility (v0.2.1-rc.2)

The `0.2.1` line added a plugin admission gate: before a profile imports a
bundle, DSH checks that b

undle's `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` against the single runtime

version and skips the bundle
when any declared range does not match (prereleases participate in ran

ge
matching). A plugin that declares only the previous harness line is therefore
silently dropped at

startup with a `skipping profile bundle` line. This
release targets the current runtime line — ever

y DSH peer is
`^0.2.1-rc.2` — so the bundle is admitted. The concrete-IP bind also calls
`webServer.

getOrigin()`, which first appears in `0.2.1-alpha.3`; the peer
range deliberately excludes the earli

er alphas where that method is absent.
The host and client contracts it consumes (`webServer`, `sett

ings`,
`credentials`, `loader`, `connection`, `slots`, `locale`, and the
`settings.general.item` slo

t) are current for this release. Rebuild `lib/`
after upgrading.
## Optional: dsh-better-sidebar compatibility patch

dsh-better-sidebar's trust fence matched the connection row by the wrong
name and read the raw `!!js

` config, so its panels (explorer / editor /
terminal / git) only ever accepted loopback. The repo s

hips the fix as a
profile-level pnpm patch (no harness change):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

This copies `patches/dsh-better-sidebar.patch` into the profile's
`patches/` directory, registers it

under `patchedDependencies` in
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and runs `pnpm install`.
## Security notes

- Default is **off** (loopback). The DSH launcher itself refuses
`--host 0.0.0.0` for the same reaso
n: the listener exposes the agent's tools to the selected network. Only enable it on a trusted netwo

rk.
- The toggle is only reachable through the fenced route, and disabling from a
remote machine cut

s that machine off (expected — re-enable locally).
- `/lan-access/handoff` returns the process launc

h token, so it refuses every
non-loopback Host header: a remote LAN page never receives the token an

d
cannot mint a cookie for another authority.
- The bind survives plugin reloads and patch re-applie

s; a full process
restart re-applies the persisted value at boot.
